body: Exhale longer than you inhale for two minutes: in for 4, out for 6.
Before a nerve-racking call, write your first sentence on a sticky note.
When your chest tightens, press your feet into the floor and count five slow breaths.
Ask of one fear today: what's the most likely outcome, not the worst one?
Hold a cold glass of water in both hands and notice the temperature for 30 seconds.
Do one small thing you've avoided out of nerves. Notice the dread was bigger than the task.
Rate your anxiety 0 to 10 now and again in 20 minutes. Feelings crest and fall on their own.
Write what you'd actually do if the thing you fear happened. A plan shrinks the fear.
Replace "what if" with "even if" once today, then finish the sentence.
Relax your jaw, drop your shoulders, and unclench your hands. Check again at lunch.

When your heart races, name it plainly: this is adrenaline, and it passes.
Hum one low note for a full exhale. The vibration helps slow your breathing.
Skip one reassurance check today. Sit with the not-knowing for five minutes.
Keep a "predicted vs. actual" note: what you feared, then later what really happened.
Walk briskly for 12 minutes when anxiety spikes. Give the energy somewhere to go.
Put a hand on your chest and breathe so it rises under your palm, six times.
Sort today's worries into two columns: can act on, can't act on. Act on one.
When a worry shows up after 9pm, jot it on a notepad by the bed and let paper hold it.
Ask of one worry: will this matter in five days, five months, or five years?
Turn one worry into a question you can answer with a single next step.
Give a recurring worry a silly nickname. The fifth rerun is harder to take seriously.
Check the news once today, at a set time, and close the app after.
Drop your shoulders away from your ears right now. Stress tends to live two inches too high.
Pick one obligation this week to cancel, postpone, or hand off. Do it today.
Take a five-minute walk without your phone between two tasks.
Sigh on purpose: two short inhales through the nose, one long exhale through the mouth. Three times.
Write down the three things stressing you most, then circle the one you control.
Eat lunch away from your desk today, even if it's only 15 minutes.
Tense your fists for five seconds, then let go. Work up from hands to shoulders.
Put a 10-minute buffer between meetings in today's calendar.
Put on one song you love and do nothing else for its length.
Before replying to a stressful email, stand up and get a drink of water.
Say "this is a stressful moment" to yourself. Naming it gives you a half-step of room.
Clear one flat surface at home. A small patch of order calms a busy head.
Stretch your neck slowly side to side for one minute at 3pm.
Lower one standard today. Store-bought is fine, and so is a shorter email.
Spend 10 minutes near trees or plants today. A park bench counts.
During your next stressful task, check your breath. If you're holding it, let it out.
Pick a wake-up time and keep it tomorrow, weekend or not.
Dim the lights at home an hour before bed tonight.
Keep your bedroom a little cool tonight, around 65 to 68 degrees.
Charge your phone outside the bedroom tonight. A cheap alarm clock does the job.
Have your last coffee by 2pm today. Caffeine lingers longer than it feels like it does.
Write tomorrow's to-do list before bed so your brain doesn't rehearse it at 2am.
Save your bed for sleep. Scroll, work, and worry somewhere else.
Take a warm shower an hour or two before bed. The cool-down afterward nudges sleepiness.
If you nap today, keep it under 30 minutes and before 3pm.
Read a paper book for 15 minutes in bed instead of a screen.
Set a wind-down alarm for 45 minutes before bedtime.
Finish heavy meals two to three hours before bed tonight.
If you wake at 3am, don't check the time. Clock-watching feeds the alertness.
Block the light at your bedroom window tonight, even with a towel over the gap.
Go to bed when you're sleepy, not just when the clock says so.
Log two numbers each morning this week: bedtime and wake time. Patterns show up fast.
Try a body scan in bed: notice your toes, then feet, then ankles, all the way up.
Skip the nightcap tonight. Alcohol makes the second half of the night's sleep lighter.
Do one thing for five minutes that used to bring you joy, even if it doesn't feel fun yet.
Act first, feel later: take the shower before deciding if you're up to it.
Open the curtains as soon as you're up.
Rate your mood 1 to 10 before and after a short walk. Let the data argue with the gloom.
Put away five things and count it as a real win.
Eat something at a regular mealtime today, even if you're not hungry.

Tell one trusted person, "I'm having a heavy day." You don't need to explain more.
When your mind says "nothing will help," treat it as a symptom talking, not a fact.
Plan tomorrow with one pleasant thing and one useful thing, each 10 minutes long.
Sit by a window for 15 minutes this morning with your coffee or tea.
Brush your teeth even on a hard day. Small care is still care.
Write down three things you did today, however small. Getting up counts.
Ask someone to come along on a short errand. Company makes it easier to go.

Put on music with a beat while you do one chore.
Stand in sunlight for five minutes around midday.
Check what you've eaten and drunk today before blaming yourself for a bad mood.
